business_summary: Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders is a defence shipbuilder. FY26 net profit was Rs 2,583 crore, with Rs 2,858 crore over the last four quarters and no loss-making quarters. Revenue grew 18.4% a year over three years, and operating margin is 17.4%.
why_own: The case rests on strong revenue and profit growth, a wider operating margin, high returns on capital and almost no debt. FY26 operating cash flow was negative despite positive profit, and the P/E is about 40% above its own 5-year median, so the thesis depends on earnings converting to cash. No supplied documents were available, so there are no qualitative drivers.

drivers.statement: Revenue keeps compounding at a double-digit rate (3-year CAGR currently 18.4%, 5-year 26.3%). (warn line tightened by code from 12 to 12.91.)
Operating margin holds most of its recent expansion (17.4% in FY26, up 7.2 percentage points over three years).
Returns on capital stay high (ROCE 32.5%, ROE 29.2%), so growth is earning well above a typical cost of capital. (warn line tightened by code from 22 to 22.71.)
The balance sheet stays nearly debt-free (debt/equity 0.05x, interest cover 44.8x), leaving room to fund growth without financial strain. (warn line tightened by code from 0.3 to 0.07.)
Cash conversion: operating cash flow should cover at least half of reported profit. (added by code: currently -1.03.)
Trailing P/E should not sit more than 30% above its own 5-year median. (added by code: currently 39.87.)

kill_criteria.description: Operating margin falls below 10%, which would reverse most of the three-year expansion.
ROCE falls below 15%, so the high-return premise no longer holds.
More than one loss-making quarter in the last four.

risks.statement: Cash from operations was negative in FY26 (about -1.03x net profit) even though net profit was positive. The cause is not in the evidence and is untested, but profit is not yet turning into operating cash.
Valuation is demanding: trailing P/E is 27.1x, about 40% above its own 5-year median of 19.4x, and price/book is 7.95x. Any slowdown in growth or margin could be punished.
The 7.2 percentage point margin gain over three years may not persist. The evidence does not say what drove it, so whether it is durable is untested.
Revenue growth over three years (18.4% CAGR) is slower than over five years (26.3%), so the growth rate may be easing.

skeptic_counter_case: The thesis would be wrong if FY26's profit is not turning into cash and margins are giving back their gains. Operating cash flow was -1.03x profit. Management blames a Navy advance received in March 2025 being spent, which means earlier cash was customer-funded, not earned. The margin thresholds are lenient: the warn line of 13% allows about 60% of the 7.2pp gain to reverse, and the 10% kill line is roughly the level three years ago. Provisions on Coast Guard orders and a fixed-price ONGC contract add execution risk. At 27.1x P/E against a 19.4x median, there is little room for error. What would change this view: Reported operating cash flow covering at least half of net profit over a full year, with operating margin staying above 13%, would show that earnings are converting to cash and that the margin gain is durable.
